body:
## Problem

The current template `scripts/setup-npm.mjs` documents that npm trusted publishing requires npm >= 11.5.1, but the fallback/success logic can still leave the workflow below that requirement:

- The curl fallback installs `https://registry.npmjs.org/npm/-/npm-11.4.2.tgz`, which is below the documented trusted-publishing minimum.
- If all install strategies fail, the script treats any npm major >= 11 as acceptable, even when the version is 11.0.0-11.5.0.
- The script does not re-check the final npm version against >= 11.5.1 before returning success.

npm's docs currently state that trusted publishing requires npm CLI 11.5.1 or later and Node.js 22.14.0 or higher:

https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers

## Downstream Evidence

While fixing link-foundation/lino-objects-codec#31, the JavaScript release run showed the same setup path failing to upgrade npm on GitHub Actions:

- Run: https://github.com/link-foundation/lino-objects-codec/actions/runs/25286485840
- Log evidence: bundled npm 10.9.7 failed with `Cannot find module 'promise-retry'`, then setup printed `Updated npm version: 10.9.7` and continued to publish.
- The publish later failed with npm E404/access/trusted-publisher symptoms.

## Reproduction

1. Use the current template `scripts/setup-npm.mjs`.
2. Force the standard npm install path to fail, so the curl fallback runs.
3. Observe that the fallback installs npm 11.4.2, which is below the documented trusted-publishing minimum.
4. Alternatively, make all fallback strategies fail while the current npm is any 11.x below 11.5.1; the script accepts it by major version only.

## Suggested Fix

- Parse versions numerically and enforce npm >= 11.5.1, not just major >= 11.
- Enforce Node.js >= 22.14.0 before publish setup.
- Resolve the latest npm 11.x >= 11.5.1 from registry metadata for the tarball fallback instead of pinning 11.4.2.
- After all strategies, re-run `npm --version` and fail if the result is still below 11.5.1.

This is the approach being applied downstream in link-foundation/lino-objects-codec#32.
title: setup-npm.mjs should enforce npm >= 11.5.1 after fallbacks

body:
# Upstream report: `publish-to-npm.mjs` retries permanent failures and there is no first-publish bootstrap path

Target repository: `link-foundation/js-ai-driven-development-pipeline-template`

Discovered while fixing `link-assistant/web-search#11`. Two related problems in
the npm release path cause a brand-new package's **first release to fail** and
make the failure slow and hard to diagnose.

---

## Problem 1 — Permanent failures are retried `MAX_RETRIES` times and surfaced as a generic error

### Where

`scripts/publish-to-npm.mjs`

```js
const FAILURE_PATTERNS = [
  'packages failed to publish',
  'error occurred while publishing',
  'npm error code E',
  'npm error 404',
  'npm error 401',
  'npm error 403',
  'Access token expired',
  'ENEEDAUTH',
];
// ...
for (let i = 1; i <= MAX_RETRIES; i++) {
  console.log(`Publish attempt ${i} of ${MAX_RETRIES}...`);
  const { success, error } = await attemptPublish(/* ... */);
  if (success) { /* ... */ return; }
  if (i < MAX_RETRIES) {
    console.log(`Publish failed: ${error.message}, waiting ${RETRY_DELAY / 1000}s before retry...`);
    await sleep(RETRY_DELAY);
  }
}
console.error(`❌ Failed to publish after ${MAX_RETRIES} attempts`);
process.exit(1);
```

Every detected failure is treated as retryable. But `npm error 404` (first
publish of a package that does not exist yet) and `401`/`403`/`ENEEDAUTH`/
`Access token expired` are **permanent** — retrying cannot help.

### Reproducible example

Run the release workflow for a scoped package that has never been published and
without a configured trusted publisher / token. Observed (from
`link-assistant/web-search` run 27448599744):

```
npm error code E404
npm error 404 Not Found - PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/@scope%2fpkg - Not found
The requested resource '@scope/pkg@0.8.1' could not be found or you do not have permission to access it.
...
Publish attempt 1 of 3...
Publish attempt 2 of 3...
Publish attempt 3 of 3...
❌ Failed to publish after 3 attempts
```

~28 seconds are wasted on retries, and the final message hides the real cause.

### Workaround

Set a real `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN` (see Problem 2) so the first publish succeeds; this
sidesteps the retry path but does not fix the misclassification.

### Suggested fix

Classify non-retryable patterns and exit immediately with actionable guidance:

```js
const NON_RETRYABLE_PATTERNS = [
  'npm error 404', 'npm error 401', 'npm error 403',
  'e404', 'e401', 'e403',
  'access token expired', 'eneedauth',
  'you must be logged in', 'unable to authenticate',
];

function isNonRetryableFailure(output) {
  const lower = output.toLowerCase();
  return NON_RETRYABLE_PATTERNS.some((p) => lower.includes(p));
}
```

In the retry loop, when `error?.nonRetryable` is set, print guidance that
explains the first-publish bootstrap and exit `1` without retrying. Reference
implementation: `js/scripts/publish-to-npm.mjs` in
`link-assistant/web-search` PR #12.

---

## Problem 2 — No first-publish bootstrap path (OIDC cannot create a new package)

### Where

`.github/workflows/release.yml` — the `Publish to npm` steps run
`node scripts/publish-to-npm.mjs` with `id-token: write` but **no**
`NODE_AUTH_TOKEN`. They rely solely on npm OIDC trusted publishing.

### Why it fails

npm trusted publishing requires a *trusted publisher* to be configured on
npmjs.com, which can only be done for a package that **already exists**. The
first publish of a brand-new package therefore cannot use OIDC and fails with
E404 (see Problem 1). The template's documented "just push and it releases"
flow is broken for the very first release of any new package.

### Suggested fix

Add an optional token bootstrap fallback on the publish steps:

```yaml
- name: Publish to npm
  id: publish
  env:
    NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}
  run: node scripts/publish-to-npm.mjs --should-pull
```

When `NPM_TOKEN` is set, the first publish succeeds; once the package exists and
a trusted publisher is configured, OIDC takes over and the token can be removed.
This keeps OIDC as the steady-state mechanism while unblocking bootstrap.
Document that `NPM_TOKEN` is only needed for the first release.
title: publish-to-npm.mjs retries permanent failures and there is no first-publish bootstrap path

body:
## Summary

`.github/workflows/release.yml` has **no top-level `permissions:` block**. The file goes straight from `on:` to `concurrency:`, so every job inherits the repository's default `GITHUB_TOKEN` scope — which on many organisations is still read/write-all.

This matters more here than in an ordinary workflow: `release.yml` is the file that publishes packages, pushes tags and commits, and creates releases, so it is the highest-value token in the repository.

## Reproducible check

```bash
gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/contents/.github/workflows/release.yml --jq .content \
  | base64 -d | grep -n '^permissions:' || echo "NONE"
# -> NONE
```

Then compare against the effective grant:

```bash
gh api repos/OWNER/REPO/actions/permissions/workflow --jq .default_workflow_permissions
# -> "write" on organisations that have not changed the default
```

Any workflow step — or any compromised third-party action, all of which float on mutable major tags here — then runs with write access to repository contents.

## Suggested fix

Add least-privilege at the top of the file and escalate per job only where needed:

```diff
 on:
   push:
     branches: [main]

+permissions:
+  contents: read
+
 concurrency:
```

Then, on the jobs that genuinely need more:

```yaml
  release:
    permissions:
      contents: write      # create tags/releases
      id-token: write      # trusted publishing / attestations
```

`link-assistant/formal-ai` applies exactly this pattern (`release.yml:32-33`, with per-job escalation) and its release pipeline works unchanged.

## Workaround

Organisation owners can set **Settings → Actions → Workflow permissions → Read repository contents** as the default, but that is repo-external configuration that a template consumer will not inherit when they generate a new project from this template. The fix belongs in the template so every generated repository is safe by default.

## Scope

Filed against all three pipeline templates (`rust-`, `js-`, `python-`); verified missing in each. Discovered while auditing CI/CD against these templates in link-assistant/formal-ai#796.
title: release.yml has no top-level permissions: block, so jobs inherit the default GITHUB_TOKEN scope

body:
## Summary

In `.github/workflows/release.yml`, both manual-dispatch jobs are declared with **no `needs:` at all**:

```yaml
  instant-release:
    name: Instant Release
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.release_mode == 'instant'
```

```yaml
  changeset-pr:
    name: Create Changeset PR
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && github.event.inputs.release_mode == 'changeset-pr'
```

(lines 527-529 and 646-648 at the current `main`.)

Because a job with no `needs:` starts immediately and in parallel with every other job, `instant-release` runs its full publish sequence — version bump, commit to `main`, `npm publish` via OIDC trusted publishing, GitHub release — while `lint` and `test` are still running, or even after they have failed. The workflow run is then marked failed, but the package is already on the registry and the version commit is already on `main`. npm does not allow republishing that version, so recovery means a deprecate/unpublish plus another bump.

This contradicts the pipeline's own best-practice #9 ("validated releases only"), which every other release path in the template does follow: the automatic `release` job is correctly gated on `needs: [lint, test]`.

## Reproduction

1. Generate a repository from this template.
2. Introduce a deliberate failure, e.g. add `const x =;` to a source file, or make a unit test assert `false`.
3. Push it to `main`.
4. Run the workflow manually: **Actions -> Release -> Run workflow**, with `release_mode: instant` and `bump_type: patch`.

Observed: `lint` and `test` go red, and `instant-release` publishes the broken code to npm anyway.
Expected: `instant-release` never starts once a quality gate has failed.

## Workaround

Only trigger `release_mode: instant` from a commit whose CI is already green, and check the run of that exact SHA first. This is a policy, not a control — nothing in the workflow enforces it.

## Suggested fix

Add the dependency and gate on the dependency *results*, not merely on job completion. `needs:` alone is not sufficient here: `detect-changes` is skipped on `workflow_dispatch`, and a skipped dependency skips its dependents unless the condition survives it (see [actions/runner#491](https://github.com/actions/runner/issues/491)). `!cancelled()` keeps the condition evaluable while still stopping the job when the run is cancelled.

```yaml
  instant-release:
    name: Instant Release
    needs: [lint, test]
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      github.event.inputs.release_mode == 'instant' &&
      needs.lint.result == 'success' &&
      needs.test.result == 'success'
```

```yaml
  changeset-pr:
    name: Create Changeset PR
    needs: [lint]
    # A changeset PR does not publish, so it only waits on the fast lint gate.
    if: >-
      !cancelled() &&
      github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' &&
      github.event.inputs.release_mode == 'changeset-pr' &&
      needs.lint.result == 'success'
```

Note the block scalar: `if: !cancelled() && ...` written on a single line is invalid YAML, because a plain scalar may not begin with `!` (the tag indicator).

## Context

Found while auditing CI/CD false positives and false negatives in a repository seeded from this template: link-foundation/browser-commander#75. The fix above is applied there in link-foundation/browser-commander#76.
title: Manual release jobs have no `needs:`, so an instant release publishes to npm without lint or tests

body:
`scripts/sanitize-npm-userconfig.mjs` removes the deprecated `always-auth` key but
keeps the `_authToken` line that `actions/setup-node` writes. When a project has no
`NPM_TOKEN` secret and relies on OIDC trusted publishing, that leftover line makes
npm believe it is already authenticated, so it never performs the OIDC exchange and
the registry rejects the anonymous upload with a misleading `E404`.

**Reproduction**

1. Generate a project from this template; do not set an `NPM_TOKEN` secret.
2. Configure a trusted publisher for the package on npmjs.com.
3. Trigger the release workflow.

The publish step fails with:

```
npm error code E404
npm error 404 Not Found - PUT https://registry.npmjs.org/<package>
```

and every step of the job shows `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX` in its
environment, even though the workflow sets no token. The npm user config at
`$NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG` contains
`//registry.npmjs.org/:_authToken=${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`.

**Root cause**

`actions/setup-node` with `registry-url` unconditionally writes that line and
exports the placeholder — see actions/setup-node#1440 and #1551. The fix
(actions/setup-node#1558) shipped only on the v7 line; `@v6` still contains the
placeholder in `dist/setup/index.js`.

**Workaround**

Strip the line after `setup-node` and before `npm publish`:

```bash
sed -i '/_authToken/d' "$NPM_CONFIG_USERCONFIG"
```

**Suggested fix in code**

Extend `sanitize-npm-userconfig.mjs` to remove the `_authToken` line as well,
unless a real credential is present. A token is "real" only when it is non-empty
and is neither `XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX-XXXXX` nor an unexpanded `${NODE_AUTH_TOKEN}`:

```js
const AUTH_TOKEN_LINE = /^[^\S\r\n]*(?:\/\/[^\s=]*:)?_authToken[^\S\r\n]*=.*(?:\r?\n|$)/gim;

export function sanitizeNpmrc(content, { keepAuthToken = false } = {}) {
  const withoutAuthToken = keepAuthToken ? content : content.replace(AUTH_TOKEN_LINE, '');
  return withoutAuthToken.replace(ALWAYS_AUTH_LINE, '');
}
```

It is also worth failing fast with actionable guidance when neither a usable token
nor OIDC request variables (`ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` /
`ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_TOKEN`) are available, so the failure names the missing
configuration instead of surfacing a bare `E404`. Moving the template to
`actions/setup-node@v7` fixes the root cause too, but the sanitiser change is
version-agnostic and protects projects that are still pinned to `@v6`.

A working implementation, with tests, is in
`js/scripts/prepare-npm-auth.mjs` of link-foundation/meta-language (PR #192).
title: sanitize-npm-userconfig.mjs leaves the setup-node placeholder _authToken, breaking OIDC trusted publishing

body:
## The principle

> On `main`, the job of CI/CD is not to test the code — it is to produce a release.
> If a credential needed to publish any planned artifact is missing, expired or
> unauthorised, **no expensive work should run at all**: fail immediately, at the
> top of the graph, before the first build minute is spent.

Reported from a real incident in [`link-foundation/box#117`](https://github.com/link-foundation/box/issues/117):
a release run was **green** while publishing nothing. The Docker Hub token had
expired, the login step was tolerant (by design — [box#82](https://github.com/link-foundation/box/issues/82)),
every push step was `skipped`, the run concluded `success`, and the registry
kept serving a three-month-old image. The failure was discovered by a human
looking at Docker Hub, not by CI.

The principle is being added to hive-mind's CI/CD best practices as
[link-assistant/hive-mind#2221](https://github.com/link-assistant/hive-mind/issues/2221)
("Prove You Can Publish Before You Build"). The reference implementation is
[`link-foundation/box#118`](https://github.com/link-foundation/box/pull/118):
a `preflight-credentials` job that every release job depends on, which in
*release mode* (`push` to `main`) fails the run before any build starts, and in
*report mode* (pull requests) reports without blocking — because on a PR the job
of CI **is** to test the code.

## What actually proves a credential works

Measured against both registries while writing box#118 — the results are
counter-intuitive, so please do not shortcut them:

| Check | Verdict |
| --- | --- |
| Secret is non-empty (`[ -n "$TOKEN" ]`) | **Proves nothing.** An expired token is non-empty. This is the check that let the box incident through. |
| Token endpoint returns 200 | **Proves nothing.** `ghcr.io/token` returns HTTP 200 and a token for *any* scope without verifying it can be granted — the token it hands back is your own credential, base64-encoded. `auth.docker.io` answers an **anonymous** `pull,push` request with 200, silently narrowing the `access` claim to `pull`. |
| `docker login` succeeds | Proves authentication, not authorisation. It does not prove the account may write *this* repository. |
| An **attempted write** | The only proof. `POST /v2/<repo>/blobs/uploads/` → `202` + a `Location` header means the registry accepted a write session; `DELETE <Location>` cancels it. `403 permission_denied` is the honest answer a token-endpoint 200 hides. |

The shape of the probe (about 20 lines of `curl`), the release/report split and
the tests are in [box#118](https://github.com/link-foundation/box/pull/118) —
[`scripts/release/registry-probe.sh`](https://github.com/link-foundation/box/blob/issue-117-9b4bd99dda25/scripts/release/registry-probe.sh)
(the write probe) and
[`scripts/release/preflight-credentials.sh`](https://github.com/link-foundation/box/blob/issue-117-9b4bd99dda25/scripts/release/preflight-credentials.sh)
(the release/report gate) are directly portable.

## Where this template has the same defect

Line numbers against `338fafa` (2026-09-05), `.github/workflows/release.yml`.

**npm is already right, and is the model to copy.** `release` (line 446) and
`instant-release` (line 555) both request `id-token: write` (lines 468, 575) and
publish with OIDC trusted publishing; `NODE_AUTH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.NPM_TOKEN }}`
(lines 533, 615) is documented as a bootstrap fallback only. Nothing there can
expire silently.

**Docker Hub is the gap.**

* `docker-publish-config` (line 637) `needs: [release, instant-release]` (line 639)
  — Docker publishing is ordered **after** the npm publish, so the Docker Hub
  credential is first exercised when the version is already immutable on the
  registry.
* `DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` reaches the pipeline at lines 663 (config job env), 717
  (per-architecture build push) and 757 (the manifest push login).
* `scripts/check-docker-publish.mjs` is the only credential check, and it is a
  presence test: `if (!token) errors.push('DOCKERHUB_TOKEN is required …')`
  (line 78 of that file, `if (!token)` at line 77). An **expired** token is a non-empty string and passes
  it — which is exactly how box#117 happened.

### Concrete failure

`DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` expires. A change lands on `main`. `lint` and `test` run, the
`release` job publishes `1.4.0` to npm (immutable, cannot be retracted after 72h),
`docker-publish-config` reports `enabled=true` because the secret is non-empty,
`docker-publish-build` spends both native runners building two architectures, and
only then does `docker/login-action` fail. Result: npm has `1.4.0`, Docker Hub
does not, the GitHub Release advertises a `docker pull` that 404s, and the fix
requires a whole new version because `1.4.0` can never be re-released. A preflight
would have failed the run in ten seconds, before the npm publish.

### Trusted publishing status

| Artifact | Today | Available |
| --- | --- | --- |
| npm | ✅ OIDC (`id-token: write`) | — |
| Docker Hub | ❌ `secrets.DOCKERHUB_TOKEN` | OIDC trusted publishing (`docker/login-action` with `permissions: id-token: write`, the **organization** name as `username`, no `password`, and `DOCKERHUB_OIDC_CONNECTIONID`). Note: Docker Hub OIDC connections are organization-scoped, so a personal namespace still needs a token — which makes the preflight probe the mandatory part, and OIDC the improvement where the image lives under an org. |
## Suggested change

1. **Add a `preflight-credentials` job** that runs first on `main` and that every
   publishing job (and every expensive build job) declares in `needs:`.
   * Release mode (`push` to `main`): a missing or refused credential **fails the
     run immediately**, naming every problem in one report rather than the first
     one.
   * Report mode (`pull_request`): the same probe runs and reports, but never
     blocks — a fork PR legitimately has no publishing secrets.
2. **Probe with a write, not with a presence test.** See the table above.
3. **Prefer trusted publishing (OIDC) wherever the registry supports it**, so
   there is no long-lived credential to expire in the first place. Per the box
   maintainer: *"we should prefer trusted publishing, where no regular tokens
   update is necessary if possible."*
4. **Verify visibility as well as existence.** box#117 also found the published
   packages were private, so every documented `docker pull` failed for everyone
   but the publisher. Anonymous discrimination: token `401` = private,
   manifest `404` = missing, manifest `200` = published, `429` = unknown (never
   count a rate-limited probe as a pass).

Happy to open the PR here if the approach is agreed.
title: CI/CD: prove the release can be published before building it (preflight credentials on main)

body:
Found against template commit `4c8644fb457b65933fcb19b033e60e7d0338f2ad404` during [command-stream #209](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/issues/209).

`scripts/preflight-credentials.sh` counts `ACTIONS_ID_TOKEN_REQUEST_URL` being set as verified npm publishing access. That variable exists even when the npm trusted-publisher configuration is wrong. A successful unrelated Docker probe can leave the overall preflight green without making any authenticated request to npm.

Offline reproduction with stubbed HTTP (no network, no real credentials):

```bash
python3 experiments/issue-209/probe-template-preflight.py
```

[Probe](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-209-4043f0c126d5/experiments/issue-209/probe-template-preflight.py), [output](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-209-4043f0c126d5/dev/log/issues/209/pulls/210/validation/template-preflight-before.log.gz): `2 verified, 0 failed, 0 unknown`, exit 0, and zero npm package exchange requests.

Workaround: perform a package-specific npm exchange before considering the npm target verified; require every configured target to pass independently.

Suggested fix: request GitHub's JWT with audience `npm:registry.npmjs.org`, POST to `/-/npm/v1/oidc/token/exchange/package/<escaped-package>`, reject HTTP/network/malformed responses and discard the returned token without logging it. This is the flow used by [npm CLI](https://github.com/npm/cli/blob/latest/workspaces/libnpmpublish/lib/oidc.js) and [trusted publishing](https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers/). [Implementation and denied-exchange tests](https://github.com/link-foundation/command-stream/blob/issue-209-4043f0c126d5/.github/scripts/publish-preflight.mjs).
title: Release preflight marks npm OIDC verified without checking the package token exchange

body:
## Summary

In every new repository created from this template, the first push to `main` fails the release preflight with a message that doesn't say what to do:

```
FAIL: npm OIDC package exchange rejected (404); configure a trusted publisher or bootstrap token
##[error]release-preflight: npm OIDC package exchange rejected (404); configure a trusted publisher or bootstrap token
```

(konard/voice-simulator `main`, run 39021393361, job "Release Preflight".)

npm's OIDC exchange answers 404 in two different situations, and each needs a different maintainer action:

1. **The package has never been published.** npm can attach a trusted publisher only to an existing package, so "configure a trusted publisher" cannot be done yet. The only fix is an `NPM_TOKEN` repository secret for the first release. After that, add the trusted publisher and delete the secret.
2. **The package exists but has no trusted publisher for this repository and workflow.** The fix is the package's trusted publisher settings.

The current message names neither the secret's settings URL, nor the npm access page, nor which case applies. For a repository fresh from the template it is always case 1, and "configure a trusted publisher" sends the maintainer to a page that can't help.

## Suggested fix (applied and verified in konard/voice-simulator#4, commit d64bf2d)

On a 404 without `NPM_TOKEN`, look up the public package document (`GET $NPM_REGISTRY/<package>`) and report the matching action:

```sh
# The exchange answers 404 both for an unpublished package and for a package
# without a trusted publisher. The public package document tells them apart,
# so the failure names the maintainer action that fixes this repository.
explain_npm_exchange_404() {
  local package="$1" name repo secrets access status
  name=$(node -e 'process.stdout.write(decodeURIComponent(process.argv[1]))' "$package" 2>/dev/null)
  repo="${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-this repository}"
  secrets="${GITHUB_SERVER_URL:-https://github.com}/${GITHUB_REPOSITORY:-OWNER/REPO}/settings/secrets/actions"
  access="https://www.npmjs.com/package/${name}/access"
  status=$(http "$NPM_REGISTRY/$package")
  status="${status##*"$NEWLINE"}"
  case "$status" in
    404)
      bad "npm has no package ${name} yet, and npm configures trusted publishing only for published packages. Add an NPM_TOKEN repository secret (a granular token allowed to publish ${name}) at ${secrets} for the first release, then add a trusted publisher for ${repo}, workflow release.yml, at ${access} and delete the secret"
      ;;
    200)
      bad "npm rejected the OIDC exchange for ${name} (404): add a trusted publisher for ${repo}, workflow release.yml, at ${access}"
      ;;
    *)
      bad "npm rejected the OIDC exchange for ${name} (404) and the package lookup answered ${status:-no status}: add a trusted publisher at ${access}, or an NPM_TOKEN repository secret at ${secrets} if the package was never published"
      ;;
  esac
}
```

and call it in place of the generic `bad` in the `404)` branch of `check_npm_oidc`. Tests in `tests/release-preflight.test.js` use the existing curl stub (`tests/fixtures/preflight-stub/curl`, extended to answer the package lookup) and cover all three branches.

The `SKIP: NPM_TOKEN is not set ... (NPM_TOKEN is the documented bootstrap fallback, issue #77)` line also cites an issue number from another repository's history. It could say what the fallback is for: "NPM_TOKEN is the bootstrap fallback for a package npm does not have yet".

References:
- npm trusted publishing: https://docs.npmjs.com/trusted-publishers
- `npm trust` prerequisites list "the package must already exist on the npm registry": https://unpkg.com/npm@11.11.1/docs/content/commands/npm-trust.md
title: Release preflight fails every fresh fork with 'npm OIDC package exchange rejected (404); configure a trusted publisher or bootstrap token' without saying which action applies
